review_notes:
I read all 112 lines of the target file. I also checked the definitions of `cutoffHeatGram`, `cutoffHeatGramEquiv` and `cutoffHeatGramAt` (ActualHeatGrams.lean, HeatGramEvolution.lean) and every use of `dyadicHeatGram_coe`, `cutoffHeatGram_time_congr` and `dyadic_radius_square_succ`. The uses are in this file, SupportedHeatEnvelope.lean and DyadicHeatAt.lean, where `cutoffHeatGram_time_congr_at` copies the same pattern.

The main simp-interface gap is a missing rewrite lemma for the next dyadic Gram, the one at index `i + 1`. Every decrement proof needs that Gram written at the time `(R / 2 ^ i) ^ 2 / 4` of the current scale, and each proof rebuilds that equation by hand.

I did not flag `dyadicHeatGram_coe` for lacking `@[simp]`. It is an `rfl` unfolding of a definition, and every caller already uses it explicitly through `simp only` or `rw`, so adding `@[simp]` would not clearly help.

`dyadic_radius_square_succ` should stay out of the default simp set. Its left-hand side, `(R / 2 ^ (i+1)) ^ 2`, is not a canonical form, and the default simp set may already rewrite it through `pow_succ` or `div_pow`.

I found no rewrite cycles and no competing simp rules. I could not run Lean, so the proposed lemma's proof and the rewrite order in the shortened proofs (`rw` of the `i + 1` lemma before `dyadicHeatGram_coe`) have not been compiled.

findings.problem: There is one coercion lemma, `dyadicHeatGram_coe`, and it writes the index-`i` Gram at time `(R / 2 ^ i) ^ 2`. The decrement statements compare index `i` with index `i + 1`, so a proof needs the `i + 1` term at time `(R / 2 ^ i) ^ 2 / 4`. The file gives no lemma with that normal form. `cutoffHeatGram_time_congr` only applies when the user supplies the time equation and both positivity proofs; its hypothesis `hst : s = t` cannot be found by simp, so it is useless as a simp lemma. As a result, `dyadicHeatGram_lower` (lines 72–77) and `dyadicHeatGram_upper` (lines 101–105) each repeat the same three-line `have hnext := cutoffHeatGram_time_congr … (dyadic_radius_square_succ R i)` and then `simp only [..., dyadicHeatGram_coe]; rw [hnext]`. The same block appears again in SupportedHeatEnvelope.lean. In DyadicHeatAt.lean it appears twice, after a word-for-word copy of the congruence lemma named `cutoffHeatGram_time_congr_at`. That copy exists only because the pole here is fixed as the section variable `p`.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a lemma whose output is the normal form the callers actually need, for example:

theorem dyadicHeatGram_succ_coe {R lambda : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (hlambda : 0 < lambda) (i : ℕ) :
    (dyadicHeatGram μ hQ hk U χ hR hlambda (i + 1) : Euclidean n →L[ℝ] Euclidean n) =
      cutoffHeatGram μ hQ hk χ.weight.continuous (χ.hasCompactSupport μ hQ) U
        (div_pos (sq_pos_of_pos (div_pos hR (show 0 < (2 : ℝ) ^ i by positivity))) (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 4)) p lambda := by
  rw [dyadicHeatGram_coe]
  exact cutoffHeatGram_time_congr μ hQ hk U χ _ _ (dyadic_radius_square_succ R i)

In both decrement proofs, delete the `hnext` block and use `rw [dyadicHeatGram_succ_coe, dyadicHeatGram_coe]` before `simp only [sub_apply, inner_sub_right]`. The `i + 1` lemma goes first so the general coercion lemma does not catch that term. Separately, generalise `cutoffHeatGram_time_congr` over the pole (an explicit `x : X` instead of the section variable `p`). Then DyadicHeatAt.lean can reuse it instead of keeping `cutoffHeatGram_time_congr_at`.
findings.benefit: With this lemma, a single rewrite puts the decrement `G_i - G_{i+1}` into the form that `dyadic_heat_increment_lower_mass`, `gaussian_dyadic_heat_increment_envelope` and `dyadic_heat_increment_upper_bound` expect, namely heat Grams at times `s^2` and `s^2/4`. Callers would no longer need to restate positivity side proofs and the radius identity. That removes four copies of the same block across three files, and a later change to the time parametrisation would only need updating in one place.
